correctness.rationale: After z=lambda*w, the chain rule on w^r Q(w^d) gives the stated residue and degree. For r=0, ordinary Rolle intervals account for every root of Q' with the retained endpoint factor; Q'(0)/Q(0) is the negative sum of reciprocal roots counted with multiplicities. If r>0, the weighted polynomial u^(r/d)Q(u) adds the interval from zero to the first positive root. Those disjoint intervals and the endpoint multiplicity exhaust the new degree, so the interior roots are simple and a lost endpoint root cannot return; constant reduced polynomials cause no exception. The core is a subset of the shadow by definition in Hägg–Shapiro I (p. 4); their Theorem 1.4(i) supplies connectedness and containment of the vertices. These facts and finite-level localization force every interior point of every spoke and the center, by separation of the leaves. The frozen text's shorthand attribution of the subset inclusion to (i) is harmless with the definition. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/branches/replay_exact_audit.py 5 used explicit binomial/factorial coefficients, exact endpoint division and Sturm counts for 567 descendants; the uploaded checker was only inspected. The arbitrary orders and d follow from proof, not the replay.
residual_risks: The limiting-core argument uses the published connected-core theorem rather than reproving it here; no claim for perturbed polygons.

This finding of demonstrable coverage is not a claim about first discovery or historical priority: the indexed comparator has a later catalogue path date, and the priority chronology of the authors' Part III copy is not established here.
